# Check — M0-a-06, transactions: closing check of session fix round S6 (lane check/M0-a-06-close-s6, 2026-10-13)

**Verdict: PASS.** This checker re-ran the four required lines of round S6 (J340 (2), `docs/M0-FIX-QUEUE.md` Q54,
`checks/M0-a-06-notes.md` N-c1-5, N-c1-6) with its own evidence and found each one fixed. No new finding is a blocker.
In short:

* **The fix.** Split restoration in `relevel.ts` `restoreSplit` (§2.2 rule 3 (c)) now bounds the restored level by
  every row finer than the vertex that one of its two run edges carries and the other does not: a finer chain that ends
  at the vertex along the run. This is the round's only source change (`src/tx`: one file, 5 code lines and 4 comment
  lines against `main`).
* **The fourteen sequences** now commit encodable, readable arenas. On this checker's own build, every committed arena
  of the 52 220-batch probe encodes, and `routeLines` reads every live chain. On the pre-round line, the encoder refuses
  51 batch states across the 14 sequences (15 with the regression's duplicate), and `routeLines` throws on 33 states
  across 9 of them. After the round, both counts are 0.
* **The shift is confined.** Every batch's outcome is identical before and after. The 51 940 lines outside the 14
  sequences are byte-identical. The 92 lines that differ are all inside the 14 sequences, each from that sequence's
  first broken batch on.
* **Refusals.** tx refuses exactly as before on every family (registered 59 / 336, 104 / 384, 49 / 220). The encoder's
  refusals drop 14 sequences → 0.
* **Mutants.** 19 targeted mutants were run against NEAR, and 6 of them against the golden too. Every mutant aimed at the new bound is killed or equivalent, except N8. N8 is an instance of a
  pre-existing gap (N12) in pinning the changed-face list, so it is not this round's blocker: notes N-s6c-2.

Four new findings go to the notes:

* **N-s6c-1** routes a LAWFUL refusal class to the session. In the wide families, 9 `remove lane` batches are refused by
  index freshness. The cause is the vertex that N-s6-1 keeps at L1, so N-s6-1's "fails safe" is incomplete. The class
  is identical before and after this round.
* **N-s6c-2** and **N-s6c-3** are hardening notes.
* **N-s6c-4** is a record-keeping completion.

## Method

* **Before-image.** The pre-round sources come from `main` (`00095cb0`) through the GitHub contents API (`gh api`,
  raw; no git). The last commit of `relevel.ts` there is `0fde16fe`, R6. Fetching every `src/tx` and `test/tx` file and
  comparing with the tree gives this diff: `src/tx/relevel.ts` differs, and nothing else in `src/tx` does. In `test/tx`,
  `fuzz.test.ts`, `removals.test.ts` and `support.ts` differ, and `readable.test.ts` is new.
* **Mirrors** under `scratchpad/waves/check-M0-a-06/`. Each is a whole copy of `plat/` (no `dist`) with its own
  `node_modules` (`install --frozen-lockfile --offline`, exit 0).
  * `after`: the tree. `diff -rq` against the tree is clean.
  * `pre`: `after` with `main`'s `relevel.ts` swapped in.

  Every mutant was restored and `cmp`-checked against the tree. Every probe file was removed after use.
* **Probes** (scratch only, never in the tree):
  * `zz-check-s6-golden.test.ts`: per batch, the outcome (code and detail); sha of the record; sha of `bits(p)` (every
    column, the slots, the handles and the index's mutable state); `encodeArena`'s outcome (sha of the refs and bytes, or
    its error); and `routeLines` of every live non-indexed chain (sha, or the failing chains). On top of those, this
    checker's own whole-arena constancy scan: every vertex interior to a level-r run, r = 1 … 4, has exactly two edges
    of level ≤ r, of one level, with identical rows of r's class. Where a reader or the scan fails, it also records
    `allProblems`.
  * `zz-check-s6-shift.test.ts`: every live vertex (x, y, level, flags) after every batch of the 14 sequences.
  * `zz-check-s6-rec.test.ts`: the record's per-level created / changed lists, by face key.
  * `zz-check-s6-idx.test.ts`: the state at a refused `remove lane`.
  * `mutants.py` and `mutgolden.py`: the targeted mutants against NEAR, and against the golden.

## (3) New findings, judged by the blocker rule

No blocker. Notes appended to `checks/M0-a-06-notes.md` under "Round S6 — the closing check's notes":

* **N-s6c-1** (LAWFUL refusal, routed to the session). The wide families hold 9 `remove lane` refusals by index
  freshness: `an L2 batch wrote the L1 index (delete of vertex N (L1)) outside its promotions and demotions`. They are
  along ×104 729 seeds 325 @12 and 1097 @9 / 12 / 15, and heavy ×15 485 863 seeds 7 @18, 9 @6, 247 @5, 619 @19 and
  719 @14. They are identical before and after S6, and none falls in the registered families. In the two this checker
  examined (325, 247), the refused vertex is an L1 `split` vertex on one way whose two edges differ only by an L2 kerb
  ending there. That is N-s6-1's 'kept' vertex. Removing the kerb then dissolves an L1 vertex in an L2 batch. J290:
  LAWFUL, MAKE-IT-SUCCEED. N-s6-1's "the outcome fails safe" is therefore incomplete.
* **N-s6c-2** (hardening). The restored vertex's changed-face levels are unpinned (N12, N8).
* **N-s6c-3** (hardening, with N-s6-2). (c)'s `single` row comparison is unpinned (D1).
* **N-s6c-4** (record). Heavy 210 has two broken batches and two shifted vertices, not one. C-0356's "one vertex per
  sequence" lacks (606, 1943) at batch 15. A single-seed `insert way` role-consistency refusal (`branches`, along 648
  @13) is also unclassed in the author's census.
